title: m-pseudo-coherence in distinguished triangles of ring complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $m$ an integer, and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. Call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Let $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D(R)$. If $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $B$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent; if $A$ and $C$ are $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $B$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent; and if $B$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Apply the compatible finite-free approximation triangle theorem to hA,hB. It gives a distinguished source triangle S with finite-free third vertex Q(E), and phi:S -> T whose first two components have the witness homology conditions.

Build the five-term homology ladder in degree i from phi.comm1, phi.comm2 and naturality of the connecting map. Mathlib homologySequenceComposableArrows5_exact gives exactness of both rows. For i>m, the first component is epi (i=m+1 uses the boundary epi; larger i uses an iso), the second and fourth are iso, and the fifth is mono. Apply the five lemma to get an iso on the third component. At i=m, delete the first vertex of the five-term ladder and apply the four lemma with epi on H^m(phi2), epi on H^{m+1}(phi1), and mono on H^{m+1}(phi2). This gives epi on H^m(phi3). Transport along S.obj3=Q(E); E and phi3 form the required witness.

For clause (2), rotate twice to C -> A[1] -> B[1]. Shift compatibility changes m-pseudo-coherence of A to (m-1)-pseudo-coherence of A[1], and m=(m-1)+1 for C. Apply clause (1) at m-1 and shift back. For clause (3), rotate once to B -> C -> A[1], apply clause (1) at m, and shift back. Mathlib rot_of_distTriang supplies distinguishedness of both rotations.
